cards.back: A number that names equal parts of a whole.
The top number. It tells how many parts you have.
The bottom number. It tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Fractions that name the same amount.
A fraction whose numerator and denominator have no common factor except 1.
A familiar fraction used to compare, such as 0, 1/2 or 1.
The same denominator for two or more fractions.
A fraction with a numerator of 1.
Decide which fraction is greater, or whether they are equal.
All of the equal parts together. The fractions you compare must refer to the same whole.

cards.front: How do you make an equivalent fraction?
cards.back: Multiply (or divide) the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

cards.front: Two fractions have the same denominator. Which is greater?
cards.back: The one with the greater numerator.

cards.front: Two fractions have the same numerator. Which is greater?
cards.back: The one with the smaller denominator, because its pieces are larger.
Each third is cut into 2 smaller pieces. There are twice as many pieces, and each is half the size.

cards.front: How can you tell if a fraction is more than 1/2?
cards.back: The numerator is more than half of the denominator.

cards.front: Why must fractions refer to the same whole when you compare them?
cards.back: Half of a large pizza is more than half of a small pizza.
6/8. Multiply top and bottom by 2. 4/5 comes from adding 1, which changes the value.

cards.front: Which is in simplest form: 4/6 or 5/6?
cards.back: 5/6. Both parts of 4/6 can be divided by 2.

cards.front: Is 1/8 greater than 1/6 because 8 is greater than 6?
cards.back: No. Eighths are smaller pieces than sixths, so 1/8 < 1/6.

cards.front: Is 2/3 = 3/4 because you add 1 to the top and bottom?
cards.back: No. Adding the same number does not make an equivalent fraction. Multiply instead.
